requirement: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents not to raise mechanical changes to new text as questions. For text that was already agreed or that the user supplied, it MUST direct agents to show the change as a diff against that text, followed by a list of the mechanical changes.
rationale:
The requirement sets two obligations on the text of the `habeas-requirements` skill. (1) It must direct agents not to raise mechanical changes to new text as questions. (2) For text already agreed or supplied by the user, it must direct agents to show a diff against that text, followed by a list of the mechanical changes.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_shows_mechanical_changes_without_asking]` is marked `{test}`. It calls `assert_phrases` on the bundled `habeas-requirements` skill. `assert_phrases` calls `assert_text` on the output of `bundled_skill`. I did not read `assert_text` or `bundled_skill` directly. I relied on the stored evidence record's description that the skill text is whitespace-collapsed and that each phrase must be present. The test asserts two phrases:
- "Show text that was already agreed or that the user supplied as a diff against that text, then a \"Mechanical:\" list of the changes" covers obligation 2: the diff, then the list.
- "Don't raise mechanical changes to new text as questions" covers obligation 1.

Both phrases appear in `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md`, in Workflow step 4. The requirement is about what the skill text directs, so phrase assertions on the skill are the right check. The requirement has no conditional behavior beyond these two directives, so no input class or boundary goes untested. The assertions would fail if either directive were removed or reworded. I found no gaps.
